brief.subject: IRS will take card payments directly under final rules
brief.headline: IRS Finalizes Rules to Accept Card Tax Payments Without Third-Party Processors
brief.dek: New IRS card-payment rules, a Connecticut preparer charged over 4,335 returns, and state tax fights in Colorado, Washington and California.
brief.lede: Final IRS regulations let the agency accept credit and debit card tax payments directly, with no third-party processor in the middle.

sections.heading: IRS can take your card directly
bullets: Final regulations let the IRS accept credit and debit card tax payments itself, bypassing third-party processors.
The rules implement changes from the Taxpayer First Act, which could simplify how owners pay federal tax bills.
They also lift restrictions on the IRS paying fees under contracts tied to card-based tax payments.

sections.heading: Preparer charged over 4,335 returns
bullets: 4,335 allegedly fraudulent returns were filed with the IRS through a Connecticut tax business, authorities say.
Former owner Yuridia Trujillo, 43, of Meriden, has been arrested.
The case is a reminder to verify who prepares your returns and review what gets filed.

sections.heading: State tax fights heat up
bullets: Colorado: A Denver judge ruled Wednesday a graduated income tax measure can stay on the November ballot.
That measure would replace Colorado's flat rate, though the legal challenge against it continues.
Washington: Gov. Bob Ferguson warns repealing the new millionaires tax would make childcare less affordable.
California: Meta struck a stock deal to keep CEO Mark Zuckerberg in-state if a billionaire wealth tax passes.

items.title: Rule: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. The final regulations reflect changes to the law made by the Taxpayer First Act that would allow the IRS to directly accept payments of tax by credit or debit card, without having to connect taxpayers to third-party payment processors. These final regulations affect consolidated groups and their members.
